item.title: OPEC+ set to keep oil output policy unchanged on Sunday, sources say
item.description: OPEC+ is set to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OPEC+ is set to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps. The meeting comes as the Iran war continues to disrupt oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting [USN:L6N44D030 TEXT:"OPEC+'s influence"] over prices and market share. Unlike in the past, the group's supply decisions have had a limited impact on the market. In August, OPEC+ agreed its production boost for September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. Despite the agreed production increases, the group made up of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, including Russia, still produces far below its targets because of the war. OPEC+ still has another layer of production cuts in place, covering most members of the 21-country group until the end of 2026. Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas. This debate will likely happen later in 2026 and hence OPEC+ is likely to [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"pause its output increases"] for the fourth quarter, sources earlier told Reuters.

item.title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
item.description: About 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China’s main border crossing with Nepal.
item.dc:creator: Nicoco Chan, Tingshu Wang
item.content:encoded: About 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China’s main border crossing with Nepal. The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on August 26. Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organized for foreign media by China's foreign ministry. There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster, video and pictures from the scene showed. The only structure still visible from before the mudslide was a portion of a nearby water tower installation. Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood. Behind hazard signs that read “Danger Area Pass Quickly”, three groups of about 20 rescue and recovery workers dug the earth using shovels while several red excavators stood by on Sunday afternoon. COMPLICATED OPERATION Rescue workers have divided the search area into seven zones, officials told Reuters. They have completed searches in four of them, with three remaining. The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing. On Saturday, emergency crews in Nepal rescued a [USN:L4N44X01J TEXT:"Chinese worker"] who had been in a tunnel linked to a hydropower station. On China's side of the border, 31 people had been confirmed dead while 531 others were still classified as missing as of Friday. Among those still unaccounted for are 261 foreigners from 23 countries, Chinese officials have said. Gyirong County sits at an average altitude of more than 4,000 meters, though the port itself lies lower, at around 1,800 meters. The risk of landslides, poor weather and deep mud has further complicated rescue and recovery efforts. The only land route into Gyirong was restored by Wednesday morning, allowing China to bring in heavy equipment to aid recovery and eventual rebuilding. State media has shown workers restoring power to the area by sinking temporary electric poles to reconnect it to the grid. HINDU PILGRIMAGE SITE Gyirong has emerged as the main border crossing for travelers and trade between Nepal and Tibet over the past decade, after a 2015 earthquake in Nepal badly damaged an alternative crossing farther east. The port was shut down between July last year and January because of an earlier glacial flood. In addition to a shipment point to Nepal for Chinese goods, including electric cars, it had also become a crossing point for thousands of Hindu pilgrims in recent years. Many Hindus travel through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a high-altitude site in Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati. Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said. There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing.

item.title: All Blacks suffer another injury setback
item.description: New Zealand will have to do without another of their starters for next weekend’s final match against South Africa after Luke Jacobson was added to the injury list following Saturday’s defeat in the third test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand will have to do without another of their starters for next weekend’s final match against South Africa after Luke Jacobson was added to the injury list following Saturday’s defeat in the third test. Jacobson has an elbow injury and joins captain Ardie Savea and centre Quinn Tupaea, who will miss out on the trip to Baltimore in the United States for the last international of the All Blacks' South Africa tour. It will be played next Saturday. Savea dislocated a shoulder in the first half of Saturday’s 29-24 defeat to the Springboks at Soccer City in a major blow to Kiwi hopes while centre Tupaea sustained a knee ligament tear, All Blacks officials said. South Africa, who lead the series 2-1, head to the U.S. without star winger Cheslin Kolbe, who broke his jaw in Saturday’s clash.

item.title: Germany plans anti-sabotage shield after airport drone attack, Bild reports
item.description: Germany is planning a broad package of measures to strengthen its defences against drone attacks, cyber intrusions and other forms of Russian sabotage following a failed airport drone attack last month, Bild am Sonntag newspaper reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany is planning a broad package of measures to strengthen its defences against drone attacks, cyber intrusions and other forms of Russian sabotage following a [USN:L8N44U0IR TEXT:"failed airport drone attack"] last month, Bild am Sonntag newspaper reported on Sunday. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told the newspaper that Russia's hybrid attacks had become a part of daily reality. "These attacks will increase, but we can defend and protect ourselves," he was quoted as saying. Russia has long rejected allegations it is carrying out operations in Western Europe and has denied involvement in the German airport attack, saying it will respond to what its foreign ministry spokesperson called "anti-Russian action". According to Sunday's newspaper report, which cited the German interior ministry, police mobile drone defence capabilities would be expanded under the plan, with rapidly deployable counter-drone units stationed in cities to protect the airspace above critical transport hubs and government districts. Companies operating critical infrastructure, such as power utilities and defence manufacturers, would be granted the legal authority to not merely detect drones but also actively fend them off, it added. A national protective shield, or "cyberdome", would be established, involving a network of digital sensors designed to detect and intercept attempted hacking attacks. The government also intends to expand the use of AI-supported technologies, biometric facial recognition and video surveillance, for example at railway stations, to identify suspected attackers preparing acts of sabotage. The interior ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on the report.

item.title: MLB roundup: Kyle Schwarber homers, Phillies beat East-leading Braves
item.description: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday. The Phillies evened the four-game series at one win apiece and moved within four games of the first-place Braves in the National League East. Schwarber had two hits for Philadelphia, as did Bryce Harper, Derek Hill and Luis Arraez. Wheeler (12-5) struck out nine while allowing one run and three hits. Atlanta, which had won nine of its last 11, managed only five hits, including solo homers from Ronald Acuna Jr. and Austin Riley. Braves starter Martin Perez (8-9) gave up four runs and seven hits in 3 2/3 innings. Dodgers 6, Nationals 5 Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as Los Angeles rallied to beat visiting Washington. Teoscar Hernandez had an RBI single in the first inning as the Dodgers earned their third victory in three days without Shohei Ohtani. Edman was occupying Ohtani's leadoff spot, while Hernandez replaced Ohtani as designated hitter. Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow tied a season high by allowing four runs over six-plus innings but didn't factor into the decision. Left-hander Alex Vesia (2-1) pitched one inning to earn the win and Tanner Scott pitched the ninth for his 21st save. Cubs 6, Marlins 5 Ian Happ drove in two runs, and Michael Conforto slugged a solo homer as Chicago defeated host Miami. The Cubs will go for a three-game sweep of the Marlins on Sunday. Ryan Zeferjahn got the final five outs without allowing a run to earn his first save with the Cubs and fifth of the season. Conforto's homer was the major league-leading 200th of the season for the Cubs. Griffin Conine led Miami with a two-run homer measured at 430 feet in the fifth inning. Kyle Stowers added the longest home run of his career, a 442-foot solo blast, in the seventh. Giants 9, Mets 5 Christian Koss and Rafael Devers both hit two homers to help visiting San Francisco beat New York in the middle game of a three-game series. Anthony Molina (3-0) and five relievers combined on a five-hitter for the Giants, who halted a two-game skid. Devers homered in the first and fifth innings, giving him six in the last six games, while Oslevis Basabe and Grant McCray each homered in the final two innings. Molina allowed just one hit over his five innings. A.J. Ewing hit a two-run homer and Brett Baty had three RBIs for the Mets, whose two-game winning streak ended. Rookie Zac Thornton (3-5) was roughed up for six runs on seven hits in five innings. Red Sox 5, Orioles 0 Sonny Gray pitched seven scoreless innings to earn his major league-leading 17th win as Boston won its third straight against host Baltimore. The Red Sox can sweep the four-game series Sunday. Gray (17-4), who was facing Baltimore for the first time this season, held the Orioles to three hits and three walks while striking out seven. Baltimore finished with five hits, struck out 10 times and collected three doubles. Chris Bassitt (6-5) went 5 2/3 innings and was charged with three runs in the loss. Tigers 6, Guardians 0 Riley Greene had four RBIs in his ninth career multi-homer game, and Framber Valdez (9-10) pitched a season-high-tying seven scoreless innings as visiting Detroit downed Cleveland. All-Star rookie Parker Messick (11-9) had a career-high 12 strikeouts over six innings and allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks for the Guardians, who won both games of a doubleheader in walk-off fashion on Friday. Ben Malgeri had three hits and an RBI, and Gleyber Torres and John Peck added two hits apiece for the Tigers, who outhit Cleveland 11-3. Angels 6, Pirates 1 Yusei Kikuchi pitched six scoreless innings for his first win of the season and Josh Lowe hit a home run to lead Los Angeles over host Pittsburgh to end a three-game losing streak. Wade Meckler doubled twice and had two RBIs, Zach Neto went 3-for-5 with an RBI, and Mike Trout added two hits and an RBI for Los Angeles. Making just his 10th start of the season after missing almost four months with left shoulder inflammation, Kikuchi (1-5) picked up his first win since Sept. 24, 2025. Bryan Reynolds went 3-for-3 with a home run and a walk and Rafael Flores Jr. had two hits, including a double, for Pittsburgh. Braxton Ashcraft (14-6) took the loss. Reds 5, Brewers 3 Matt McLain's home run in the seventh inning broke a tie and host Cincinnati defeated Milwaukee following a rain delay of almost 2 1/2 hours in the fourth. Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also homered for the Reds, who have won three of their last four. Tony Santillan (3-4) got the win despite giving up a run in his only inning and Emilio Pagan pitched the ninth for his 21st save. William Contreras homered for the Brewers, who had won three of their previous four. Aaron Ashby (13-3), who gave up McLain's home run, was the loser. Twins 6, White Sox 4 Ryan Jeffers belted a three-run homer to push Minnesota to a win over host Chicago, leveling the three-game series at one win apiece. Kaelen Culpepper went 2-for-5 with a double, two runs and an RBI for the Twins, who also got RBIs from Kody Clemens and Brooks Lee. Minnesota right-hander Taj Bradley (11-6) allowed four runs on four hits in five innings. Right-hander Yoendrys Gomez pitched a scoreless ninth for his 21st save. Munetaka Murakami hit a two-run homer to lead the White Sox. Colson Montgomery added a solo home run, and Miguel Vargas drove in a run. Left-hander Anthony Kay (9-8) gave up five runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings. Rays 6, Rangers 3 (10 innings) Jonathan Aranda blasted a three-run homer in the 10th inning to lift Tampa Bay to a win against host Texas in Arlington. Junior Caminero and Richie Palacios also homered to back starter Drew Rasmussen, who limited the Rangers to one run and three hits over seven innings. Tyler Wells (4-2) pitched a scoreless ninth and 10th to earn the win. Rangers right-hander Jacob deGrom allowed two runs and four hits over six innings. He struck out seven and walked one. Joc Pederson and Evan Carter homered for the Rangers, who have lost three of four. Closer Jacob Latz (3-2) took the loss. Blue Jays 4, Royals 3 Kazuma Okamoto's fourth hit of the night was a tiebreaking, seventh-inning RBI single, and Toronto made it hold to win their fourth straight, beating host Kansas City to move above .500 for the first time since early April. Okamoto's game-winning hit came after an error by Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. extended the inning. Okamoto drove in two runs and Lukes had three hits with an RBI while Mason Fluharty (6-1) threw a scoreless inning to get the win, which moved the Blue Jays (72-71) into a tie with the Cleveland Guardians for the final American League wild-card spot. Salvador Perez had two hits with an RBI and John Rave homered for Kansas City, which has lost five of six. Kansas City's Seth Lugo gave up three runs on eight hits over five innings, while Toronto's Max Scherzer allowed three runs over 5 2/3 innings. Diamondbacks 4, Astros 3 (10 innings) Gabriel Moreno stroked a one-out RBI single to center field in the top of the 10th inning and Arizona rallied to defeat host Houston. The Diamondbacks squared the three-game interleague series after Moreno plated automatic runner Ildemaro Vargas with his single off Astros reliever Bryan King (2-4). Brandyn Garcia notched his fifth save. Starter Brandon Pfaadt allowed three runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings. Jonathan Loaisiga (7-3) pitched a scoreless ninth. Isaac Paredes (three RBIs) singled in consecutive at-bats -- the first to give the Astros a 2-0 lead in the third and the second to rebuild that two-run margin with a two-out hit in the fifth. Rookie starter Ethan Pecko gave up one run on five hits over 4 1/3 innings. Yankees 5, Padres 1 Cody Bellinger's two-run single capped a four-run second inning and Carlos Rodon threw five solid innings as visiting New York knocked off San Diego. Rodon (5-3) allowed two hits and one run, walking three and tying a season high with seven strikeouts. Four relievers finished off the game for New York (81-61), which was anchored by Ben Rice's three hits and two walks. Padres starter Robbie Ray (11-8) was denied in his third try for his 100th career win, lasting only 2 1/3 innings and yielding five runs off five hits and four walks. It was the left-hander's shortest start since August 2024. The Padres, who managed just three hits, scored their only run on Manny Machado's 25th homer, making him the only player with 25-plus homers in each of the last 11 seasons (excluding the COVID-shortened 2020 season). Rockies 10, Cardinals 7 Cole Carrigg, Adael Amador and Ezequiel Tovar had two hits apiece and Colorado rallied to beat St. Louis in Denver. Joshua Baez and Ivan Herrera homered and finished with two hits each for St. Louis, which lost ground in the National League wild-card chase. The Cardinals are four games behind Arizona for the final NL playoff spot. Brennan Bernardino (4-3) got the win and Jordan Romano picked up his 15th save for Colorado. Cardinals starter Matthew Liberatore (5-14) retired the first 10 batters before the Rockies scored six in the fifth inning. Athletics 6, Mariners 2 Jeffrey Springs pitched seven scoreless innings to win for the first time since April 14 as the Athletics prevailed, further damaging host Seattle's dwindling playoff hopes. Max Muncy and Lawrence Butler homered for the A's, who have won four in a row and will go for a sweep of the four-game series Sunday afternoon. Springs (4-13), who dropped 13 straight decisions after opening the season 3-0, allowed two hits, walked two and struck out six. The Mariners lost their third in a row and are seven games behind division-leading Houston and six back in the chase for the AL's third and final wild-card berth with 19 to play. Seattle starter George Kirby (9-11) gave up four runs (three earned) on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: US carrier Abraham Lincoln departs Thailand after respite visit
item.description: The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln left Thailand on Sunday after a five-day port visit, ending a respite from an extended deployment that included operations in the Middle East, the U.S. Navy said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln left Thailand on Sunday after a five-day port visit, ending a respite from an extended deployment that included operations in the Middle East, the U.S. Navy said. “We would like to thank the people of Thailand for their incredible hospitality,” U.S. Navy Captain Dan Keeler, the Abraham Lincoln’s commanding officer, said in a statement. Naval deployments typically last for six to nine months, but during times of conflict that can be extended. The nuclear-powered Lincoln, with roughly 5,000 personnel, was involved in the U.S. [USN:L8N44N1OO TEXT:"naval blockade"] and combat operations in the war with Iran and — according to Democratic lawmakers — set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea. Accompanied by other U.S. naval vessels, the Lincoln arrived early on Wednesday in Thailand, the United States' only treaty partner in [USN:L1N44M08V TEXT:"mainland Southeast Asia"], during a visit that Thai officials said would last five days. Busloads of sailors and Marines wearing civilian clothes, many smiling and waving, started arriving at a hotel in the resort city of Pattaya, about 150 km (93 miles) southeast of Bangkok, shortly after their ships docked.

item.title: Zverev reaches US Open fourth round with win over Tabilo
item.description: Top seed Alexander Zverev lost his way in the second set but got his game back under control to secure a 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 victory over Alejandro Tabilo and reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Top seed Alexander Zverev lost his way in the second set but got his game back under control to secure a 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 victory over Alejandro Tabilo and reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open on Saturday. After spending a gruelling nine hours and 26 minutes on court across back-to-back five-setters against Lorenzo Sonego and Quentin Halys, the last thing the German would have wanted was another long night on Arthur Ashe Stadium. "My coach was quite smart, he said that best-of-five sets doesn't mean that you have to play five sets. I didn't know it until now, that was quite helpful," Zverev joked later. "I'm happy with my level right now, it's going in the right direction and I'm happy to be in the second week. "I didn't practice much yesterday, only an hour, which is very little for me. I'd spent almost 10 hours on court, so I had to find my rhythm somehow. I still think I can play better, but for now I'm happy with how things are going." The 29-year-old, who won his first Grand Slam title at the French Open and finished runner-up at Wimbledon, stormed out of the blocks by breaking 25th seed Tabilo twice before taking the first set with an unreturnable serve to love. Zverev raced to a 4-2 lead in the second set but his level suddenly dropped, allowing world number 28 Tabilo to claim three games in a row and go within touching distance of drawing level in the match. However, the Chilean was unable to press home the advantage and Zverev, after chiding a courtside fan who appeared to be offering coaching advice during the ensuing tiebreak, rediscovered his composure and his best tennis, pulling away to tighten his grip on the match. The writing was on the wall for Tabilo when Zverev raced ahead 5-2 in the third, and the German booked his place in the round of 16 where 21st-seeded Italian Luciano Darderi awaits.

item.title: Les discussions entre Poutine et les émissaires américains ont été "utiles", selon le Kremlin
item.description: Vladimir Poutine a reçu samedi à Moscou les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner avec qui le président russe a tenu des discussions "très utiles", selon son conseiller diplomatique.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Antonov, Gleb Bryanski
item.content:encoded: Vladimir Poutine a reçu samedi à Moscou les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner avec qui le président russe a tenu des discussions "très utiles", selon son conseiller diplomatique. Iouri Ouchakov, qui a dit que les émissaires américains avaient "présenté un certain nombre d'idée concernant les moyens de parvenir à un accord", n'a toutefois fait mention d'aucune avancée significative après cet entretien de plus de trois heures. Vladimir Poutine a dit à Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner que la Russie effectuait de "vrais progrès" sur le champ de bataille et qu'elle était convaincue d'atteindre ses objectifs, a-t-il précisé. Le chef du Kremlin a également souligné la nécessité de s'occuper des "toutes les racines du conflit", a dit Iouri Ouchakov. "Les discussions ont dépassé un simple échange de positions afin de mettre fin à la crise ukrainienne. Des questions économiques et de possibles accords, d'importance et mutuellement avantageux, pour des projets entre la Russie et les Etats-Unis ont été abordées en détails", a indiqué le conseiller de Vladimir Poutine. "Dans l'ensemble, on peut dire que ces négociations sont arrivées à point nommé et qu'elles ont été très utiles pour chaque partie." L'émissaire russe Kirill Dmitriev a écrit sur le réseau social X que le déplacement de ses homologues américains à Moscou avait été "une importante visite pour la paix". Kirill Dmitriev et Iouri Ouchakov ont tous deux assistés aux [USN:L8N44X02W TEXT:"discussions"] entre Vladimir Poutine et les émissaires américains. Un responsable de la Maison blanche a déclaré à Reuters que les discussions avaient été "substantielles" et que les prochaines étapes seraient annoncées dans les semaines à venir. Ni Steve Witkoff ni Jared Kushner n'ont fait de commentaire à l'issue de leur entretien avec Vladimir Poutine. Ils ont quitté Moscou peu après les discussions et doivent rencontrer dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien, Volodimir Zelensky.

item.title: Tommy Edman HR lifts Dodgers to comeback win over Nats
item.description: Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Saturday. Teoscar Hernandez had an RBI single in the first inning as the Dodgers (85-57) earned their third victory in three days without Shohei Ohtani, who is out with a sore left knee and sore right biceps. Edman was occupying Ohtani's leadoff spot, while Hernandez replaced Ohtani as designated hitter. Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow tied a season high by allowing four runs over six-plus innings but didn't factor into the decision. Left-hander Alex Vesia (2-1) pitched one inning to earn the win and Tanner Scott pitched the ninth for his 21st save. Right-hander Cade Cavalli rebounded from a rough first inning to allow two runs over six innings, while retiring 16 of the last 17 batters he faced. Dylan Crews and Daylen Lile each had RBI doubles for Washington (67-77), which lost its third consecutive game. The Dodgers got off to a fast start against Cavalli after Freddie Freeman was hit by a pitch with one out in the first inning. Mookie Betts followed with a single and Hernandez singled to left for a 1-0 lead. Hunter Feduccia followed with his own RBI single for a 2-0 advantage. The Nationals pulled within a run in the second inning when CJ Abrams singled, stole second and eventually scored on a sacrifice fly from Jose Tena. A Keibert Ruiz single to right field against his former club scored Brady House and Crews followed with an RBI double for a 3-2 Washington lead in the fourth. The Nationals increased the advantage to 4-2 in the seventh inning. A Crews double knocked Glasnow from the game and Lile followed with a one-out RBI double off Vesia. After Edman's home run off Clayton Beeter (5-5) put the Dodgers up in the seventh, they added a run in the eighth when Alex Call was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded. The Nationals scored in the ninth on a Lile single and had the potential game-tying run at third with the go-ahead run at second before Scott struck out CJ Abrams to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Israeli military says it strikes southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched drones
item.description: The Israeli military said it was striking southern Lebanon early on Sunday in retaliation for Hezbollah firing two drones at Israeli soldiers stationed in a part of the region it has declared a security zone.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Israeli military said it was striking southern Lebanon early on Sunday in retaliation for Hezbollah firing two drones at Israeli soldiers stationed in a part of the region it has declared a security zone. The Israeli military had issued an evacuation warning to areas near a building in Arab Salim town in South Lebanon, saying it will strike it as it is used by Hezbollah. There was no immediate comment from the Iran-backed group. On Friday, the Israeli military said it struck weapon storage facilities intended to be used by Hezbollah in south Lebanon. Since March 2, Israeli strikes have killed more than 4,300 people in Lebanon.

item.title: Reds top Brewers after lengthy weather delay
item.description: Matt McLain's home run in the seventh inning broke a tie and the host Cincinnati Reds defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 5-3 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Matt McLain's home run in the seventh inning broke a tie and the host Cincinnati Reds defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 5-3 on Saturday night. The game featured a rain delay of almost two-and-a-half hours with two out in the bottom of the fourth. Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also homered for the Reds (68-74), who have won three of their last four. William Contreras homered for the Brewers (88-55), who had won three of their previous four. Tony Santillan (3-4) got the win despite giving up a run in his only inning and Emilio Pagan pitched the ninth for his 21st save. He escaped a bases-loaded, one-out jam. Aaron Ashby (13-3), who gave up McLain's home run, was the loser. Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott gave up two runs (one earned) and three hits in four innings without a walk and fanned five. Brewers starter Dustin May allowed two runs on five hits in 3 2/3 innings, did not walk a batter and struck out five. Both were replaced after the delay. McLain homered leading off the bottom of the seventh. He lined Ashby's 1-1 sinker to the opposite field and into the right field stands for his 15th home run. Eugenio Suarez scored from second on Grant Anderson's wild pitch in the eighth to make it 5-3. Jackson Chourio's bases-loaded sacrifice fly in the seventh had tied it 3-3 for the Brewers. Stephenson's towering homer leading off the sixth gave Cincinnati a 3-2 lead. He powered JoJo Romero's 3-1 sinker deep into the left field stands for his 15th homer. Jose Trevino's run-scoring single in the fourth tied the contest 2-2 for the Reds just after the restart following the rain delay. Luis Lara's RBI groundout in the third put Milwaukee up 2-1. De La Cruz's 22nd home run in the bottom of the first tied the game 1-1 for the Reds. Contreras' two-out solo homer in the top of the first, his 14th, gave the Brewers a 1-0 lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rockies use big 5th inning to plow past Cardinals
item.description: Cole Carrigg, Adael Amador and Ezequiel Tovar had two hits apiece, and the Colorado Rockies rallied to beat the St. Louis Cardinals 10-7 in Denver on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cole Carrigg, Adael Amador and Ezequiel Tovar had two hits apiece, and the Colorado Rockies rallied to beat the St. Louis Cardinals 10-7 in Denver on Saturday night. Brennan Bernardino (4-3) got the win and Jordan Romano picked up his 15th save for Colorado (55-87). Joshua Baez and Ivan Herrera homered and finished with two hits each for St. Louis, which lost ground in the National League wild-card chase. The Cardinals (71-72) are four games behind Arizona for the final NL playoff spot. Thomas Saggese and Leo Bernal also had two hits apiece for St. Louis. Cardinals starter Matthew Liberatore retired the first 10 batters before walking Connor Norby with one out in the fourth. He got Hunter Goodman to pop out to first and TJ Rumfield on a grounder to third to end the inning. With St. Louis leading 3-0, things unraveled in the fifth inning. Carrigg's leadoff single was Colorado's first hit, and three straight one-out singles cut the deficit to 3-2. Liberatore uncorked two wild pitches against Jake McCarthy, the second for a walk, allowing Amador to score the tying run. Luis Gastelum entered but couldn't stop the onslaught, as Tovar scored on a double steal and Norby singled to drive in McCarthy. Norby scored on Rumfield's bloop double to center to make it 6-3. Liberatore (5-14) allowed five runs on four hits in 4 1/3 innings and lost his eighth consecutive decision. He has not won since July 11th, a stretch of nine starts. St. Louis got two back in the sixth on Nolan Gorman's RBI double and a sacrifice fly by Saggese. Colorado responded in the seventh inning on Goodman's two-run single and Carrigg's run-scoring single. Goodman raced home from third on Zac Veen's squeeze bunt to cap the four-run inning. Jose Fermin had an RBI double and Herrera added a run-scoring single in the ninth before Romano recorded the final two outs. Baez's solo homer in the second and Herrera's two-run homer in the fifth, his 16th, gave the Cardinals a 3-0 lead. Rockies starter Mason Adams left after giving up a single to Alec Burleson. He allowed three runs on eight hits and struck out seven in 4 2/3 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Messi sets up Miami goal in first game since Argentina retirement
item.description: Lionel Messi provided an assist in Inter Miami's 2-2 draw with Atlanta United in Florida on Saturday in the Argentine's first appearance since retiring from international duty earlier this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lionel Messi provided an assist in Inter Miami's 2-2 draw with Atlanta United in Florida on Saturday in the Argentine's first appearance since [USN:L6N44S0US TEXT:"retiring from international "]duty earlier this week. Messi, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022 and a runners-up finish in 2026, started for Miami in a match that kicked off more than 90 minutes late due to heavy rain and lightning. The 39-year-old whipped in a corner that midfielder Casemiro headed past Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos to put Miami ahead in the 32nd minute. Miami's lead lasted only three minutes, however, as a sliding Casemiro blocked a cross that bounced off his keeper Dayne St. Clair and landed at the feet of Atlanta's Miguel Almiron, who guided it home to level. Luis Suarez restored Miami's lead just before halftime, only for Breel Embolo to convert an 87th-minute penalty and earn Atlanta a point. Messi, who scored four goals and set up another in last weekend's [USN:L4N44R00D TEXT:"7-1 rout of CF Montreal"], is joint top of the MLS scoring charts with 18 goals this season. He had previously [USN:L4N44911A TEXT:"expressed doubts"] about continuing his playing career following the death of his father, Jorge, on August 8.

item.title: Diamondbacks get past Astros in 10 innings
item.description: Gabriel Moreno stroked a one-out RBI single to center field in the top of the 10th inning and the Arizona Diamondbacks rallied to defeat the host Houston Astros 4-3 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Gabriel Moreno stroked a one-out RBI single to center field in the top of the 10th inning and the Arizona Diamondbacks rallied to defeat the host Houston Astros 4-3 on Saturday. The Diamondbacks (75-68) squared the three-game interleague series after Moreno plated automatic runner Ildemaro Vargas with his single off Astros reliever Bryan King (2-4). Brandyn Garcia notched his fifth save with strikeouts of Yordan Alvarez and Jose Altuve in the 10th. Isaac Paredes singled in consecutive at-bats -- the first to give the Astros (73-70) a 2-0 lead in the third and the second to rebuild that two-run margin with a two-out hit in the fifth. Paredes' two-run, opposite-field single to right in the third scored Yainer Diaz and Taylor Trammell. It came after Arizona right-hander Brandon Pfaadt appeared on the verge of escaping that inning unscathed by retiring Cam Smith and Jeremy Pena after Trammell pushed Diaz to third with his double to right. Pfaadt allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks with four strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings. Jonathan Loaisiga (7-3) pitched a scoreless ninth and was credited with the win. The Diamondbacks began to claw back in the fifth when Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar sandwiched singles around a Ryan Waldschmidt groundout. Nootbaar's single chased Astros rookie right-hander Ethan Pecko and advanced Tawa to third with the first of his two hits, and Geraldo Perdomo followed with a sacrifice fly to center off Enyel De Los Santos that plated Tawa and sliced the deficit to 2-1. Pecko gave up one run on five hits and one walk with two strikeouts over 4 1/3 innings. After the Astros reclaimed their two-run lead in the bottom of the fifth on Paredes' bloop single to center that scored Pena, the Diamondbacks rallied again in the seventh, this time against Kai-Wei Teng. Tawa and Waldschmidt worked successive one-out walks that prompted another pitching change for the Astros. AJ Blubaugh entered and immediately surrendered an RBI double to Nootbaar that cut the lead to 3-2, and in the top of the eighth, the Diamondbacks pulled even when Ketel Marte worked his way out of an 0-2 hole and socked a leadoff homer to right field. Marte drilled his 22nd home run, bashing a 3-2 sweeper 388 feet. Blubaugh allowed two hits over his 1 2/3 innings of relief, but both resulted in Arizona runs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jovic puts friendship with Eala on hold to win three-hour battle at US Open
item.description: Home hope Iva Jovic and Alexandra Eala of the Philippines put their friendship aside for three hours at the U.S. Open on Saturday before the 18-year-old American prevailed 7-5 3-6 7-5 at Arthur Ashe Stadium to reach the fourth round.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Home hope Iva Jovic and Alexandra Eala of the Philippines put their friendship aside for three hours at the U.S. Open on Saturday before the 18-year-old American prevailed 7-5 3-6 7-5 at Arthur Ashe Stadium to reach the fourth round. The two rising stars and close friends had already shared the court in New York during Fan Week when they teamed up with their fathers for a light-hearted doubles hit. There was little room for sentiment once the match began on Saturday, however. Jovic edged a tight opening set but Eala responded in the second, the 21-year-old raising her level to force a decider. The final set again featured momentum swings, with Jovic trailing 4-2 before fighting back to close out the victory and extend her head-to-head record against Eala to 3-0, with a win on each of the three surfaces. "That felt like a marathon. I felt like I lost my sanity five times over to win that match. But it's really worth it for this feeling," Jovic said on court. "I'm usually not one that shows that many emotions. But this one really meant a lot to me. It's everything to have another match at the U.S. Open." Jovic's victory was a welcome bright spot on a difficult day for American tennis, with Taylor Fritz, Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova among the home players eliminated. Ranked a career-high 14th, Jovic had never gone beyond the second round in two previous U.S. Open appearances but she has now reached the last 16 at three Grand Slams this season. Her victory sets up an all-American fourth-round clash with fourth seed Coco Gauff, who advanced earlier on Saturday by beating Spain's Cristina Bucsa.

item.title: Cincinnati-D.C. United match postponed due to inclement weather

item.content:encoded: An MLS match between visiting D.C. United and FC Cincinnati was postponed on Saturday night because of inclement weather. After a lightning delay of more than 2 hours and 45 minutes, the match was called off, with the following message flashed on the scoreboard. "Tonight's match has been postponed due to pitch conditions and resulting player safety concerns created by inclement weather in the Cincinnati area. The match will be played at a later date." Both teams are scheduled to play twice next week-on Wednesday and Saturday night. This was to be the first of two matches between the clubs this season. They are also scheduled to play on Oct. 24 in Washington. --Field Level Media

item.title: Timely hitting, solid pitching lift Yankees past Padres
item.description: Cody Bellinger's two-run single capped a four-run second inning and Carlos Rodon threw five solid innings as the visiting New York Yankees knocked off the San Diego Padres 5-1 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cody Bellinger's two-run single capped a four-run second inning and Carlos Rodon threw five solid innings as the visiting New York Yankees knocked off the San Diego Padres 5-1 on Saturday. Rodon (5-3) allowed two hits and one run, walking three and tying a season high with seven strikeouts. Four relievers finished off the game for New York (81-61). It stayed within four games of Tampa Bay in the American League East and maintained a 3 1/2-game lead over the Boston Red Sox for the AL's first wild-card spot. Padres starter Robbie Ray (11-8) was denied in his third try for his 100th career win, lasting only 2 1/3 innings and yielding five runs off five hits and four walks, striking out one. It was the left-hander's shortest start since August 2024. San Diego (74-68) ended the day a half-game behind Arizona for the National League's final wild-card position. The Diamondbacks (75-68) edged the host Houston Astros 4-3 in 10 innings on Saturday night. Ray sailed through the first inning on just eight pitches but found trouble in the second. Ben Rice, who collected three singles and two walks, singled to start the inning and moved up to second on a groundout by George Lombard Jr. Spencer Jones laced a two-out double to the right field corner that cashed in Rice. Then Ray lost the strike zone, issuing walks to Jose Cabellero, Austin Wells and Paul Goldschmidt, with Goldschmidt earning an RBI. Bellinger then made it 4-0 with his single to right. New York scored its final run in the third when Rice walked and Heliot Ramos singled him to third prior to Lombard's sacrifice fly that scored Rice. Manny Machado accounted for San Diego's only run when he launched his 25th homer of the year to lead off the fourth. The 391-foot blast gave him at least 25 homers in 11 straight seasons (not including the COVID-shortened 2020 campaign), the longest current streak of its kind in the majors. It was one of just three hits for the Padres. --Field Level Media

item.title: San Lorenzo vence a Talleres y vuelve al triunfo en liga argentina
item.description: San Lorenzo venció el sábado por 1-0 a Talleres de Córdoba y volvió al triunfo en el debut del director técnico provisorio Walter Perazzo, en una jornada en la cual Boca Juniors empató por 2-2 con Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: San Lorenzo venció el sábado por 1-0 a Talleres de Córdoba y volvió al triunfo en el debut del director técnico provisorio Walter Perazzo, en una jornada en la cual Boca Juniors empató por 2-2 con Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza. San Lorenzo, que días atrás quedó sin entrenador por el despido de Néstor Gorosito, se recuperó de dos partidos sin ganar y sumó la tercera victoria en la competencia. "Me encontré con un plantel golpeado que necesitaba un poco de cariño y los jugadores en estos días transmitían ganas de poder salir adelante", dijo Perazzo en conferencia de prensa. En el partido, correspondiente a la octava jornada del torneo Clausura disputado en el estadio Pedro Bidegain, el gol del triunfo lo anotó a los 63 minutos Alexis Cuello a través de un remate de cabeza. Talleres quedó con un hombre menos a los 58 minutos por la expulsión de Matías Galarza. Por su parte, Boca Juniors dejó escapar la victoria e igualó por 2-2 en su visita a Gimnasia y Esgrima después de estar dos veces en ventaja en el estadio Víctor Antonio Legrotaglie del Parque San Martín, en la provincia de Mendoza. "No podemos perder dos puntos importantes en los últimos dos minutos. Hay que ganar", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Boca Juniors, Rodolfo Arruabarrena. Los goles de Boca Juniors los anotaron Alan Velasco y Kevin Zenón a los 17 y 38 minutos, mientras que para Gimnasia convirtieron Ignacio Sabatini y Esteban Fernández a los 19 y 94, respectivamente. “Nos vamos re calientes porque nos tendríamos que haber llevado la victoria, esa es la sensación. Este empate no suma", dijo Velasco a la televisión local. En otros partidos del sábado, Vélez Sarsfield venció por 1-0 a Estudiantes de La Plata, Aldosivi ganó por 3-1 a Banfield, y Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata derrotó por 2-1 a Tigre. El viernes, Sarmiento venció 2-0 a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto, mientras que los partidos entre Belgrano-Huracán y Platense-Deportivo Riestra finalizaron igualados en un gol.

item.title: Ryan Jeffers' 3-run blast helps Twins sink White Sox
item.description: Ryan Jeffers belted a three-run homer, and the Minnesota Twins held on for a 6-4 win over the host Chicago White Sox on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ryan Jeffers belted a three-run homer, and the Minnesota Twins held on for a 6-4 win over the host Chicago White Sox on Saturday night. Kaelen Culpepper went 2-for-5 with a double and an RBI for Minnesota (68-74), which evened the three-game series at one win apiece with the rubber match set for Sunday. Kody Clemens and Brooks Lee added one RBI apiece. Munetaka Murakami hit a two-run homer to lead Chicago (74-68). Colson Montgomery added a solo home run, and Miguel Vargas drove in a run. Twins right-hander Taj Bradley (11-6) allowed four runs on four hits in five innings. He walked two and struck out six. White Sox left-hander Anthony Kay (9-8) gave up five runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings. He walked one and fanned three. Twins right-hander Yoendrys Gomez pitched a scoreless ninth for his 21st save. The White Sox wasted no time jumping to a 3-0 lead in the bottom of the first. Sam Antonacci drew a leadoff walk, and two batters later Murakami belted an opposite-field homer over the wall in left field to make it 2-0. It was the 30th homer for Murakami, who arrived in the majors this season after a standout career in Japan. Montgomery made it a three-run lead later in the inning with a homer to right. It marked his 31st homer of the season and his second in as many nights. The Twins cut the deficit to 3-2 in the fourth. Clemens grounded into an RBI fielder's choice, and Lee delivered moments later with an RBI double to left. One inning later, the Twins seized a 5-3 advantage. Ryan Kreidler was hit by a pitch, Luke Keaschall singled and one out later, Jeffers took advantage with a three-run homer to left. The 415-foot shot gave Jeffers four home runs in his past five games. Chicago pulled within 5-4 in the bottom of the fifth. Chase Meidroth singled to center, stole second base and scored on a two-out single by Vargas to left. The Twins increased their lead to 6-4 on Culpepper's RBI double in the seventh. -Field Level Media

item.title: Sonny Gray twirls 7 scoreless as Red Sox blank Orioles
item.description: Sonny Gray pitched seven scoreless innings to earn his major league-leading 17th win as the visiting Boston Red Sox defeated the Baltimore Orioles 5-0 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Sonny Gray pitched seven scoreless innings to earn his major league-leading 17th win as the visiting Boston Red Sox defeated the Baltimore Orioles 5-0 on Saturday night. The Red Sox (78-65) have won the first three games of the four-game series. The Orioles (69-74) have lost five straight. Eli White and Isiah Kiner-Falefa each drove in two runs. Trevor Story collected three hits and scored two runs and Nick Sogard had two hits for the Red Sox. Gray (17-4), who was facing Baltimore for the first time this season, held the Orioles to three hits and three walks while striking out seven. Jovani Moran, Greg Weissert and Wyatt Olds worked in relief to complete the five-hit shutout. Baltimore struck out 10 times, and three of its five hits were doubles. Chris Bassitt (6-5) matched Gray until he ran into trouble in the sixth inning. He went 5 2/3 innings and was charged with three runs on five hits and four walks. The pitchers' duel marked a second consecutive shutout for the Red Sox, who won 1-0 on Friday night. White's two-out, two-run single opened the scoring in the sixth. Connor Wong followed with an RBI single to make it 3-0. Boston, which pulled out one-run victories in the first two games of the series, stretched its lead in the seventh on Kiner-Falefa's two-out double that pushed across two more runs. The teams combined for five hits through five innings. The Orioles threatened in the third after Colton Cowser's leadoff double. He advanced to third on Jackson Holliday's lineout to right but was thrown out at home on Blaze Alexander's fielder's-choice grounder. Baltimore, which was held to six singles Friday, stranded two runners in the first inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jonathan Aranda powers Rays past Rangers in 10th inning
item.description: Jonathan Aranda blasted a three-run homer in the 10th inning to lift the Tampa Bay Rays to a 6-3 win against the Texas Rangers on Saturday evening in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Aranda blasted a three-run homer in the 10th inning to lift the Tampa Bay Rays to a 6-3 win against the Texas Rangers on Saturday evening in Arlington, Texas. The Rays had runners on the corners with one out off closer Jacob Latz (3-2) when Aranda lifted a two-strike slider over the fence in right-center field for a 6-3 lead. Junior Caminero and Richie Palacios also homered in the third game of the four-game series, and Liam Hicks had two hits and an RBI for Tampa Bay (85-57), which has won two in a row. Tampa Bay starter Drew Rasmussen limited the Rangers to one run and three hits over seven innings. The right-hander struck out seven and didn't walk a batter. Tyler Wells (4-2) pitched a scoreless ninth and 10th to earn the win. Rangers right-hander Jacob deGrom allowed two runs and four hits over six innings. He struck out seven and walked one. Joc Pederson and Evan Carter homered for the Rangers (70-73), who have lost three of four. Caminero came up with two outs in the first and homered over the left-center field fence to give the Rays a 1-0 lead. It was his 38th home run of the season, taking over the American League lead. In the fifth, deGrom got two quick outs before Palacios turned on a 2-0 sinker and pulled it over the fence in right for a home run that made it 2-0. Palacios also homered in a 7-6 win against the Rangers on Friday night. Rasmussen mostly cruised through the first five innings before Pederson dinged him with one out in the sixth, pulling a 79-mph first-pitch curveball just inside the right field foul pole to cut it to 2-1. The Rays rallied with two outs in the eighth off Jakob Junis, getting three straight singles from Aranda, Caminero and Hicks to extend the lead to 3-1. Carter got a run back in the bottom half of the inning when he greeted reliever Kevin Kelly with a leadoff home run to cut it to 3-2. The inning continued with a one-out single from Danny Jansen. Pinch runner Cam Cauley scored from first when pinch hitter Justin Foscue doubled into the left-center-field gap off reliever Cam Booser to tie it 3-3. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blue Jays top Royals, over .500 for first time in 5 months
item.description: Kazuma Okamoto's fourth hit of the night was a tiebreaking, seventh-inning RBI single, and the Toronto Blue Jays made it hold to win their fourth straight, 4-3 over the host Kansas City Royals on Saturday to move above .500 for the first time since early April.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kazuma Okamoto's fourth hit of the night was a tiebreaking, seventh-inning RBI single, and the Toronto Blue Jays made it hold to win their fourth straight, 4-3 over the host Kansas City Royals on Saturday to move above .500 for the first time since early April. With the game tied 3-3, Kansas City's Craig Kimbrel (1-3) walked George Springer, who then stole second base. With two outs, Nathan Lukes grounded to shortstop Bobby Witt Jr., whose throw pulled first baseman Vinnie Pasquantino off the bag to extend the inning. Okamoto then grounded a single to center, bringing home Springer. The Royals (63-80) put runners on first and second with nobody out in the eighth against Tyler Rogers, but Pasquantino bounced into a 1-6-3 double play and Michael Massey then grounded out to first. Louis Varland pitched a scoreless ninth for his 33rd save as the Blue Jays (72-71), who have a winning record for the first time since sitting at 4-3 on April 3, moved into a tie with the Cleveland Guardians for the final American League wild-card spot. Okamoto drove in two runs and Lukes had three hits with an RBI while Mason Fluharty (6-1) threw a scoreless inning to get the win. Meanwhile, Toronto starter Max Scherzer allowed three runs over 5 2/3 innings. Kansas City's Seth Lugo gave up three runs on eight hits and two walks over five innings. He struck out one. Salvador Perez had two hits with an RBI and John Rave homered for the Royals, who have lost five of six. Toronto opened the scoring with two outs in the first. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. singled then scored from first base on Alejandro Kirk's infield hit coupled with third baseman Josh Rojas' throwing error. Lukes then followed with an RBI single to left. The Royals answered in the bottom of the frame. Scherzer hit leadoff batter Carter Jensen, then Witt doubled to left. Jac Caglianone and Perez followed with RBI singles to tie the contest. Toronto regained the lead in the third when Lukes singled and scored from first on Okamoto's double off the third base bag. But the Royals tied it again, this time on Rave's homer just inside the right field foul pole in the fourth. Caglianone exited in the third inning due to left elbow soreness. --Field Level Media

item.title: From boardroom chic to battling win, Osaka reaches US Open last 16
item.description: Naomi Osaka continued to impress with her style and staying power at the U.S. Open on Saturday as the Japanese 13th seed shrugged off a late Achilles problem to beat Belgian Elise Mertens 6-3 3-6 7-5 and reach the fourth round.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Naomi Osaka continued to impress with her style and staying power at the U.S. Open on Saturday as the Japanese 13th seed shrugged off a late Achilles problem to beat Belgian Elise Mertens 6-3 3-6 7-5 and reach the fourth round. For her latest eye-catching [USN:L4N44T05M TEXT:"walk-on"] look, the four-times major champion blended boardroom and locker-room aesthetics in a grey checked blazer-hoodie and wide-leg pants, putting a tailored twist on traditional pre-match attire. She looked on course for a business-like win after the first set but was dragged into a battle in the third, where she had to fight through the Achilles niggle to advance. "I wouldn't say it's a huge injury," Osaka told reporters. "I'd say it's this ongoing problem that I've had since the grass season. "I don't know why it hasn't gone away. I feel I've done a lot of things in order to make it better, but maybe the time off wasn't enough. I'm not really sure what the reason is, but the medical timeout was to address that. "You know, she massaged my leg and stuff, so that seemed to help, and gave me Tylenol." The 28-year-old, a two-times champion at Flushing Meadows, reeled off three games in succession to take a 4-1 lead in the first set under the lights of Louis Armstrong Stadium, clinching it with a battling hold thanks to a string of booming serves. Osaka pushed the 23rd seed hard at the start of the next set with some heavy hitting from the baseline before pouncing with a break in the third game, only to surrender the lead by dropping the next two games. "Honestly, I can't believe I won this match," Osaka said on court after sealing victory, thanking the crowd for the energy they provided. "There was a certain point where I put my heart on the court and kept trying in every point. Thank you so much, but honestly, I'm shocked I won. I'm not going to lie." After levelling the match to force a decider, Mertens capitalised on several unforced errors by a frustrated Osaka to gain the upper hand, but there would be another momentum shift in the match after a medical timeout for the Japanese player. "I didn't play amazing and it was getting me down, sorry about my behaviour, for the little kids watching," said Osaka, who threw her racket to the floor at one point. "This is my favourite tournament. I wanted to play well in front of you. I'm just that glad I have the opportunity to play another match. "I thought I was going to be ok, but clearly I was shaky." After recovering a break late on, Osaka fired a huge ace to take a 6-5 lead and revved up her forehand in the following game to complete the win and earn a meeting with Elena Rybakina in the next round.

item.title: Rockies place ailing Willi Castro (heel) on IL
item.description: The Colorado Rockies placed infielder/outfielder Willi Castro on the 10-day injured list Saturday due to left heel inflammation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Colorado Rockies placed infielder/outfielder Willi Castro on the 10-day injured list Saturday due to left heel inflammation. The move is retroactive to Wednesday. Castro, 29, has been dealing with plantar fasciitis and hasn't played since Monday against the Baltimore Orioles. Castro has smacked a career-high 15 homers while batting .260 with 56 RBIs in 120 games this season. The versatile Castro has started 51 games at second base and 36 at third. He also has 15 starts at shortstop, six at first base and two in left field. Castro has a .247 career average with 71 homers and 284 RBIs in 825 games with the Detroit Tigers (2019-22). Minnesota Twins (2023-25), Chicago Cubs (2025) and Rockies. He was an American League All-Star in 2024 for the Twins. Colorado selected the contract of infielder Vimael Machin from Triple-A Albuquerque in a corresponding move. This is the first stint in the majors this season for Machin, who turns 33 on Sept. 25. He has a .204 career average with two homers and 15 RBIs in 116 games with the Athletics (2020-22) and Orioles (2025). Colorado also outrighted outfielder Tyler Freeman to Albuquerque after he cleared waivers to open up a 40-man roster spot for Machin. Freeman, 27, batted .247 with three homers and 23 RBIs in 79 games for the Rockies this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Yusei Kikuchi tosses 6 scoreless as Angels beat Pirates
item.description: Yusei Kikuchi pitched six scoreless innings for his first win of the season and Josh Lowe hit a home run to lead the visiting Los Angeles Angels to a 6-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Yusei Kikuchi pitched six scoreless innings for his first win of the season and Josh Lowe hit a home run to lead the visiting Los Angeles Angels to a 6-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday night. Wade Meckler doubled twice and had two RBIs, Zach Neto went 3-for-5 with an RBI and Mike Trout added two hits and an RBI for Los Angeles (54-88), which snapped a three-game losing streak. Making just his 10th start of the season after missing almost four months with left shoulder inflammation, Kikuchi (1-5) allowed five hits, walked three and struck out six to pick up his first win since Sept. 24, 2025, against Kansas City. Bryan Reynolds went 3-for-3 with a home run and a walk and Rafael Flores Jr. had two hits, including a double, for Pittsburgh (70-73). Braxton Ashcraft (14-6) took the loss after allowing three runs on seven hits in five innings. He struck out nine, threw a wild pitch and did not issue a walk. Los Angeles took a 1-0 lead in the fourth inning when Meckler doubled down the left-field line and scored one out later on a single by Moises Ballesteros. The Angels extended the lead to 3-0 in the fifth inning. Lowe led off the frame with his 11th home run, a 410-foot blast to straightaway center. Denzer Guzman followed with a single, advanced to second on a sacrifice bunt, took third on a balk and scored on Neto's single to center. Los Angeles broke the game open with three runs in the seventh inning off reliever Isaac Mattson. Adam Frazier doubled with one out and went to third on a single by Neto. Trout followed with an RBI single and Meckler then lined a double into the alley in right-center to drive in both Neto and Trout. Reynolds ended the shutout with two outs in the bottom of the eighth when he clubbed his 16th home run of the season, a 421-foot drive over the bleachers in right field. --Field Level Media

item.content:encoded: DARLINGTON, S.C. -- Inclement weather forced the cancellation of Busch Light pole qualifying at Darlington (S.C.) Raceway on Saturday evening, and no one was happier about the development than 23XI Racing's Tyler Reddick, who will now lead the field to green in the Cook Out Southern 500 to open The Chase on Sunday night (5 p.m. ET, USA Network, MRN, SiriusXM NASCAR Radio). This is the eighth time this season the five-time NASCAR Cup Series race winner and driver of the No. 45 Toyota will start from the No. 1 position on the grid -- five times through a formal qualifying session and three others as a result of a canceled session due to weather. "This is literally the best-case scenario for us," said a smiling Reddick, who has now started among the top 10 at every Darlington race throughout his entire four-year career at 23XI Racing. Reddick led 77 of the 293 laps and won from pole position here in March. "We were so strong here in the spring," he said. "Ironically enough, as I kind of got going in Cup racing, it was during COVID with no practice at all and I got very used to just having to figure it out in the first corner. "So for me, generally, I feel like we're in a really good spot most weekends when this happens. But beyond that, as strong as we were, I know teams may want to try things to close the gap, but no one had that opportunity today, so that helps us even more." Reddick will share the front row with fellow title contender Daniel Suarez in the No. 7 Spire Motorsports Chevrolet. Chase drivers, Roush Fenway Keselowski's Ryan Preece and championship leader Denny Hamlin of Joe Gibbs Racing, will roll off third and fourth. Hamlin, whose five career Darlington wins are the most in the field, won the regular-season title and starts the race with a 25-point advantage on the next-closest competitor in the 16-driver championship field. Spire Motorsports' Michael McDowell, who is not championship-eligible, will start fifth. He is followed by a pair of Chase drivers, Team Penske's Austin Cindric and JGR's Chase Briscoe, who is the two-time defending race winner and the only other multi-time winner among the field. Three non-Chase drivers -- HYAK Motorsports' Ricky Stenhouse Jr., Richard Childress Racing's Austin Dillon, and Hendrick Motorsports' Alex Bowman -- round out the top 10 on the grid. The rainout performance metric has made for an interesting challenge for several of the other Chase drivers. JGR's Christopher Bell starts 11th with Penske's Joey Logano -- a three-time series champion -- 13th on the grid. Reddick's 23XI Racing teammate Bubba Wallace will start 17th alongside Hendrick Motorsports' Chase Elliott -- tops on the grid among the three title-chasing Hendrick team Chevrolets. Hendrick's William Byron (20th), Penske's Ryan Blaney (24th), JGR's Ty Gibbs (28th), Spire's Carson Hocevar (34th) and RFK's Chris Buescher (35th) round out the Chase field on the 38-car grid. item.title: Athletics place RHP J.T. Ginn (elbow) on 15-day injured list
item.description: The Athletics placed starting pitcher J.T. Ginn on the 15-day injured list on Saturday because of a right elbow impingement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Athletics placed starting pitcher J.T. Ginn on the 15-day injured list on Saturday because of a right elbow impingement. The right-hander is eligible to come off the injured list on Sept. 20, but the Athletics haven't yet made a determination about whether he will pitch again this season. In a corresponding move, the Athletics recalled right-hander Jack Perkins from Triple-A Las Vegas one day after optioning him to the affiliate. In other moves on Saturday, the team recalled right-hander Seth Johnson from Las Vegas and optioned rookie righty Kade Morris to Triple A. Ginn, 27, last pitched on Aug. 26, earning the win after going six innings and allowing four runs, six hits (including three home runs) and two walks with three strikeouts in the 7-4 home victory over the Minnesota Twins. The Athletics flew in an orthopedist on Saturday to evaluate Ginn for what was described as general fatigue/soreness. "We'll make a determination (Saturday) as to his future," Athletics manager Mark Kotsay said Friday. "You always want guys to finish the season, but we need to make the right decision for him going forward and his future, especially going into next year." Ginn is 9-8 with a 3.71 ERA, 57 walks and 121 strikeouts in a career-high 138 1/3 innings over 27 games (24 starts) this season. He has a career mark of 14-16 with a 4.25 ERA, 97 walks and 249 strikeouts in 58 games (46 starts) over parts of the last three seasons with the Athletics. Perkins, 26, is 3-10 with a 6.50 ERA, three saves, 47 walks and 116 strikeouts in 98 1/3 innings over 33 games (13 starts) this season. He made his major league debut in 2025 and is a career 6-12 with a 5.85 ERA, six saves, 65 walks and 153 strikeouts in 137 innings over 45 games (17 starts). Johnson, who turns 28 on Sept. 19, is 0-0 with a 13.50 ERA in 4 2/3 innings over five relief appearances with the Athletics since he was traded from the Philadelphia Phillies on Aug. 3 for outfielder Colby Thomas. Johnson was 1-0 with a 5.51 ERA in 16 1/3 innings over 16 relief appearances with the Phillies. Morris, 24, was 0-1 with a 10.90 ERA, seven walks and 10 strikeouts in 17 1/3 innings over six games (two starts) for the Athletics. He started Friday's 7-6 win at Seattle and allowed five runs on five hits and one walk in 2 2/3 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indonésie-L'aéroport de Djakarta suspend les vols en raison de l'éruption de l'Anak Krakatau
item.description: Les vols aériens ont été suspendus dimanche matin au principal aéroport de Djakarta, en Indonésie, en raison des cendres volcaniques rejetées par le volcan Anak Krakatau, entré en éruption vendredi soir.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les vols aériens ont été suspendus dimanche matin au principal aéroport de Djakarta, en Indonésie, en raison des cendres volcaniques rejetées par le volcan Anak Krakatau, entré en éruption vendredi soir. L'aéroport Soekarno-Hatta a fait savoir sur le réseau social Instagram que les vols aériens seraient suspendus jusqu'à 09h30 heure locale (02h30 GMT). Quelque 209 vols, dont plusieurs internationaux, ont été affectés, a déclaré le ministère indonésien des Transports. Des nuages de cendres volcaniques ont perturbé les activités dans les provinces de Lampung, sur l'île de Sumatra, et de Banten, sur l'île de Java, a dit un porte-parole de l'agence nationale de gestion des catastrophes (BNPB). Selon la BNPB, il n'existe aucun risque de tsunami dans l'immédiat.

item.title: Guadalajara golea como visitante y sube al segundo lugar en el torneo mexicano
item.description: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, goleó el sábado por 3-0 como visitante al Atlético de San Luis y se ubicó en el subliderato del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guadalajara, el club más popular del fútbol mexicano, goleó el sábado por 3-0 como visitante al Atlético de San Luis y se ubicó en el subliderato del torneo Apertura. Con su cuarto triunfo, las "Chivas" de Guadalajara subieron del quinto al segundo lugar general con 14 puntos, dos menos que el líder América. En el partido disputado en el estadio Libertad Financiera de San Luis, el llamado "Rebaño Sagrado" se adelantó a los seis minutos cuando el guardameta Andrés Sánchez metió el balón a su propia portería tras pegarle en la espalda después de que Santiago Sandoval estrelló su remate en el poste derecho. Tres minutos después, el equipo visitante aumentó su ventaja con un disparo de zurda de Ricardo Marín en el centro del área tras un pase de cabeza de Ángel Sepúlveda. El tercer gol de Guadalajara cayó a los 80 minutos por conducto de Richard Ledezma, quien definió con un potente disparo cruzado dentro del área. "Hicimos un partido muy bueno, con una intensidad muy alta, pudimos marcar dos goles en los primeros 10 minutos, que eso ayuda para el desarrollo del partido. Los chicos lo hicieron muy bien en lo ofensivo y en lo defensivo, muchas ganas de ganar, nos vamos con una victoria de una cancha difícil", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico de Guadalajara, el argentino Gabriel Milito. "Siempre es importante empezar ganando, la voluntad siempre es la misma: pensar en el arco rival y ser un equipo valiente. A veces los rivales crean dificultades, pero el partido de hoy fue muy completo", agregó. En los otros partidos del sábado, Tigres UANL y Necaxa empataron por 1-1 con goles del uruguayo Rodrigo Aguirre y Owen González, respectivamente. Atlas y Atlante también igualaron por 1-1 con tantos del portugués Luis Esteves y del argentino Martín Sarrafiore, respectivamente. El domingo, el vigente campeón Cruz Azul enfrentará a Santos Laguna. Los encuentros entre Pumas UNAM-León, Puebla-Toluca, América-Tijuana y Querétaro-Monterrey se pospusieron debido a la participación de América, Toluca, León y Monterrey en la Leagues Cup. En el inicio de la jornada, Pachuca venció el viernes por 2-0 como visitante a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en el debut del argentino Gustavo Lema como director técnico del equipo derrotado.

item.title: Shohei Ohtani out of Dodgers' starting lineup for 3rd straight game
item.description: Shohei Ohtani was out of the Los Angeles Dodgers' starting lineup for the third consecutive game Saturday as he continues to deal with lingering issues involving his neck, right biceps and left knee.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shohei Ohtani was out of the Los Angeles Dodgers' starting lineup for the third consecutive game Saturday as he continues to deal with lingering issues involving his neck, right biceps and left knee. The superstar two-way player sat out of the Dodgers' 3-2 win on Thursday against the St. Louis Cardinals and their 5-3 win on Friday over the Washington Nationals. Ohtani, a four-time MVP, was scheduled to hit in the batting cages Saturday prior to Los Angeles' home game against the Washington Nationals, manager Dave Roberts said. How Ohtani feels afterward could determine whether the six-time All-Star ends up on the injured list. "If it doesn't feel good today," Roberts said, "then (the IL) certainly should be on the table." The 32-year-old Ohtani is batting .279 this season with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs. He is hitting just .137 (7 for 51) with one home run over his past 13 games amid the physical issues. Ohtani is 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 95 strikeouts in 85 2/3 innings across 14 starts this season. He has not pitched since July 3, and he has declined to speak to the media since Aug. 17. The minimum stint on the injured list for a two-way player is 15 days, the same as it is for pitchers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Riley Greene smacks two HRs to help Tigers defeat Guardians
item.description: All-Star outfielder Riley Greene had four RBIs in his ninth career multi-homer game as the visiting Detroit Tigers bounced back from a doubleheader sweep, beating the Cleveland Guardians 6-0 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: All-Star outfielder Riley Greene had four RBIs in his ninth career multi-homer game as the visiting Detroit Tigers bounced back from a doubleheader sweep, beating the Cleveland Guardians 6-0 on Saturday night. Framber Valdez (9-10) pitched seven scoreless innings, matching his season high, and allowed three hits. The left-hander struck out three, walked one and hit a batter in shutting down American League playoff-hopeful Cleveland (72-71). The Guardians are now tied with Toronto for the final wild-card berth after the Blue Jays beat the Kansas City Royals 4-3 later in the day, while Detroit (65-77) moved within 6 1/2 games of the spot. Greene hit two solo home runs against Parker Messick (11-9), a 407-foot drive in the first and a 421-foot blast in the sixth, breaking a homer drought that lasted more than a month. His previous homer occurred on Aug. 4 against the Seattle Mariners. Greene also scored three times. He delivered an RBI single in the third and an RBI double in the seventh, with Gleyber Torres scoring on both hits. All-Star rookie Messick had a career-high 12 strikeouts over six innings and allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks. Cleveland's Austin Peterson made his major league debut with two scoreless innings of relief. Dillon Dingler added a sacrifice fly later in the seventh, and Ben Malgeri collected his third hit with an RBI single that scored Greene and extended Detroit's lead to 6-0. On Friday, Cleveland won both games in walk-off fashion. Brayan Rocchio's homer in the ninth and Travis Bazzana's RBI single in the 10th did the honors, respectively. Rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter (right wrist sprain) was unavailable for the Guardians, but outfielder Angel Martinez and shortstop Rocchio were in the lineup after running into each other while pursuing a popup on Friday. Tigers third baseman Hao-Yu Lee started Saturday's game, telling manager A.J. Hinch that he was not bothered by the left shin contusion that resulted from his collision with Austin Hedges at home plate in the second game of Friday's doubleheader. --Field Level Media

item.title: Allemagne-L'AfD vise une victoire historique en Saxe-Anhalt
item.description: Les électeurs de Saxe-Anhalt, Land de l'est de l'Allemagne, sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour un scrutin régional lors duquel "Alternative pour l'Allemagne" (AfD) espère devenir le premier parti d'extrême droite à accéder au pouvoir au niveau régional depuis la Seconde guerre mondiale.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray
item.content:encoded: Les électeurs de Saxe-Anhalt, Land de l'est de l'Allemagne, sont appelés aux urnes dimanche pour un scrutin régional lors duquel "Alternative pour l'Allemagne" (AfD) espère devenir le premier parti d'extrême droite à accéder au pouvoir au niveau régional depuis la Seconde guerre mondiale. Mené par sa populaire tête de liste en Saxe-Anhalt - Ulrich Siegmund, 35 ans - l'AfD est crédité de plus de 40% d'intentions de vote dans le Land, avec une avance de 10 à 15 points sur la CDU, au pouvoir aux côtés du Parti social-démocrate (SPD) et du Parti libéral-démocrate (FDP). Le scrutin est suivi de près par le gouvernement de Friedrich Merz alors que l'ampleur du soutien national au parti d'extrême droite a mis en évidence la transformation du paysage politique allemand depuis la création de l'AfD en 2013. Obtenir une majorité absolue est un obstacle difficile à surmonter dans le système électoral allemand, conçu en partie pour favoriser les gouvernements de coalition et empêcher qu'un seul parti ne gouverne seul. Si l'AfD ne parvient pas à obtenir la majorité absolue, un gouvernement dirigé par la CDU, sous la houlette du ministre-président sortant Sven Schulze, est le scénario le plus probable, même si la composition exacte d'une éventuelle coalition dépendra des partis qui y participeront. Le scrutin de dimanche pourrait être suivi de plusieurs semaines de négociations de coalition. L'AFD "NE PEUT PLUS ÊTRE ARRÊTÉ" Pour l'AfD, le scrutin de dimanche est une étape décisive vers son ambition nationale, remporter les prochaines élections fédérales allemandes en 2029. "Quelle que soit l'issue du scrutin de demain, nous sommes déjà entrés dans l'histoire", a dit Ulrich Siegmund samedi soir lors d'un ultime événement de campagne. "Car ce que nous avons commencé ici en Saxe-Anhalt, ce qui est en train de se propager à travers l'Allemagne, ne peut plus être arrêté", a-t-il affirmé. Sans majorité absolue, il serait toutefois difficile pour l'AfD - qui a été classé comme un parti "extrémiste d'extrême droite" par les services de sécurité allemands - d'entrer au gouvernement. Les résultats préliminaires sont attendus dimanche aux alentours de 18h00 (16h00 GMT).

item.title: Six-time Pro Bowl S Harrison Smith returns to Vikings
item.description: Six-time Pro Bowl safety Harrison Smith agreed to return to the Minnesota Vikings for a 15th season, the team announced Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Six-time Pro Bowl safety Harrison Smith agreed to return to the Minnesota Vikings for a 15th season, the team announced Saturday. Smith, 37, had contemplated retirement in the offseason. According to reports, Smith is expected to sign a deal worth $12.25 million plus incentives that could increase his pay to $16.25 million. Smith (39 interceptions, 21.5 sacks) is one of six defensive backs in NFL history with at least 35 interceptions and 20 sacks in his career. The others are Hall of Famers Charles Woodson, Larry Wilson, Ronde Barber, LeRoy Butler and Brian Dawkins. Smith was one of the top defensive players in the second half of last decade when he earned five of his six Pro Bowl nods. His other Pro Bowl selection came in 2021. Smith has intercepted five passes in a season four times, topped 100 tackles twice and has notched three sacks on four occasions. He also had a career-best three forced fumbles in 2023. Smith has 1,180 tackles, 13 forced fumbles and 10 fumble recoveries in 207 career regular-season games (203 starts). He has 55 tackles and one sack in eight career postseason games. Last season, he had 54 tackles, two interceptions and one sack in 15 games (12 starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: Zack Wheeler stifles Braves to help Phillies level series
item.description: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday. Schwarber had two hits for Philadelphia, as did Bryce Harper, Derek Hill and Luis Arraez. Wheeler (12-5) struck out nine while allowing one run and three hits. The Phillies (80-62) evened the four-game series at one win apiece and moved within four games of the first-place Braves (84-58) in the National League East. Atlanta, which had won nine of its last 11, managed only five hits, including solo homers from Ronald Acuna Jr. and Austin Riley. Braves starter Martin Perez (8-9) gave up four runs, seven hits and four walks in 3 2/3 innings. The first three batters of the game reached against Wheeler, who escaped the jam by retiring the next three hitters. Philadelphia also put together a quick rally in its half of the first. After issuing back-to-back walks to open the frame, Perez retired Harper for the first out before Arraez's single made it 1-0. Perez then walked two of the next three hitters to force in another run. The veteran left-hander got out of the inning without further damage, but he ran into immediate trouble in the second. Hill led off with a triple and came home on Schwarber's groundout.
